questions.q: What does the reciprocity principle make people want to do?
a: Return a favor, often with something bigger
Follow the lead of a large crowd
Act fast before an offer disappears
Stay consistent with a public promise
questions.why: Lesson 1 says we feel compelled to repay, and usually give back more than we received.

questions.q: In the Cornell raffle study, what happened after Joe gave people a bottle of Coke?
a: They bought twice as many tickets as those who got nothing
They refused the bottle and avoided the raffle
They bought the same number of tickets as everyone
They asked Joe to return the bottle for cash
questions.why: Lesson 1 says the people who owed him spent 50 cents, twice what others spent on tickets.

questions.q: Why is the scarcity principle so effective?
a: We regret missing chances and act before they vanish
We trust products that few other people own
We assume expensive items must be higher quality
We copy the choices of people we admire
questions.why: Lesson 2 says regret is a powerful feeling, so limited-time offers push us to buy.

questions.q: In the beach study, what made people chase the thief?
a: They had agreed to watch their neighbor's belongings
They had been offered a reward for helping
They saw several others running after him
They recognized the thief from earlier that day
questions.why: Lesson 3 says a small commitment triggered consistency, and 95 percent of those people intervened.

questions.q: How can consistency bias help you build a habit?
a: A small commitment makes you want to follow through
Rewarding each effort keeps motivation high
Announcing a big goal attracts outside support
Removing temptations makes the habit automatic
questions.why: Lesson 3 suggests starting with mini commitments, like not hitting snooze, and letting consistency carry you.
